attributes.text: UNITED STATES PATENT OFFICE. NIKOLA TESLA, OF NEW YORK, N. Y. SYSTEM OF TRANSMISSION OF
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: ELECTRICAL ENERGY. SPECIFICATION forming part of Letters Patent No. 645,576, dated March 20, 1900. Application
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: filed September 2, 1897. Serial No. 650,343. (No model.) To all whom it may concern:
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: Be it known that I, NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing at
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: New York, in the county and State of New York, have invented certain new and
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: useful Improvements in Systems of Transmission of Electrical Energy, of which the following is a
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: specification, reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part of the same.
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: It has been well known heretofore that by rarefying the air inclosed in a vessel
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: its insulating properties are impaired to such an extent that it becomes what may be
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: considered as a true conductor, although one of admittedly very high resistance. The practical information
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: in this regard has been derived from observations necessarily limited in their scope by the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: character of the apparatus or means heretofore known and the quality of the electrical effects
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: producible thereby. Thus it has been shown by William Crookes in his classical researches, which
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: have so far served as the chief source of knowledge of this subject, that all
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: gases behave as excellent insulators until rarefied to a point corresponding to about seventy-five millimeters,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and even at this very low pressure the discharge of a high-tension induction-coil passes through
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: only a part of the attenuated gas in the form of a luminous thread or
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: arc, a still further and considerable diminution of the pressure being required to render the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: entire mass of the gas inclosed in a vessel conducting. While this is true in
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: every particular so long as electromotive or current impulses such as are obtainable with ordinary
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: forms of apparatus are employed, I have found that neither the general behavior of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: gases nor the known relations between electrical conductivity and barometric pressure are in conformity with
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: these observations when impulses are used such as are producible by methods and apparatus devised
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: by me and which have peculiar and hitherto unobserved properties and are of effective electromotive
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: forces, measuring many hundred thousands or millions of volts. Through the actions of these current
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: impulses I have been led to the discovery of certain highly important and useful facts
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: which have hitherto been unknown. Among these and bearing directly upon the subject of my
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: present application are the following: First, that atmospheric or other gases, even under normal pressure,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: when they are known to behave as perfect insulators, are in a large measure deprived
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of their dielectric properties by being subjected to the influence of electromotive impulses of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: character and magnitude I have referred to and assume conducting and other qualities which have
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: been so far observed only in gases greatly attenuated or heated to a high temperature,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and, second, that the conductivity imparted to the air or other gases increases very rapidly
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: both with the augmentation of the applied electrical pressure and with the degree of rarefaction,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the law in this latter respect being, however, quite different from that heretofore established. In
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: illustration of these facts a few observations, which I have made with apparatus devised for
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the purposes here contemplated, may be cited. For example, a conductor or terminal, to which
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: impulses such as those here considered are supplied, but which is otherwise insulated in space
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and is remote from any conducting-bodies, is surrounded by a luminous flame-like brush or discharge
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: often covering many hundreds or even as much as several thousands of square feet of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: surface, this striking phenomenon clearly attesting the high degree of conductivity which the atmosphere attains
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: under the influence of the immense electrical stresses to which it is subjected. This influence
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: is, however, not confined to that portion of the atmosphere which is discernible by the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: eye as luminous and which, as has been the case in some instances actually observed,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: may fill the space within a spherical or cylindrical envelop of a diameter of sixty
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: feet or more, but reaches out to far remote regions, the insulating qualities of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: air being, as I have ascertained, still sensibly impaired at a distance many hundred times
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: that through which the luminous discharge projects from the terminal and in all probability much
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: farther. Expressed briefly, my present invention, based upon these discoveries, consists then in producing at
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: one point an electrical pressure of such character and magnitude as to cause thereby a
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: current to traverse elevated strata of the air between the point of generation and a
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: distant point at which the energy is to be received and utilized. Referring to the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: drawing, A is a coil, generally of many turns and of a very large diameter,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: wound in spiral form about a magnetic core or not, as may be found necessary.
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: C is a second coil, formed of a conductor of much larger section and smaller
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: length, wound around and in proximity to the coil A. In the transmitting apparatus the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: coil A constitutes the high-tension secondary and the coil C the primary of much lower
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: tension of a transformer. In the circuit of the primary C is included a suitable
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: source of current G. One terminal of the secondary A is at the center of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the spiral coil, and from this terminal the current is led by a conductor B
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: to a terminal D, preferably of large surface, formed or maintained by such means as
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: a balloon at an elevation suitable for the purposes of transmission, as before described. The
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: other terminal of the secondary A is connected to earth and, if desired, also to
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the primary in order that the latter may be at substantially the same potential as
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the adjacent portions of the secondary, thus insuring safety. At the receiving-station a transformer of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: similar construction is employed; but in this case the coil A', of relatively-thin wire, constitutes
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the primary and the coil C', of thick wire or cable, the secondary of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: transformer. In the circuit of the latter are included lamps L, motors M, or other
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: devices for utilizing the current. The elevated terminal D' is connected with the center of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the coil A', and the other terminal of said coil is connected to earth and
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: preferably, also, to the coil C' for the reasons above stated. It will be observed
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: that in coils of the character described the potential gradually increases with the number of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: turns toward the center, and the difference of potential between the adjacent turns being comparatively
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: small a very high potential, impracticable with ordinary coils, may be successfully obtained. It will
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: be, furthermore, noted that no matter to what an extent the coils may be modified
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: in design and construction, owing to their general arrangement and manner of connection, as illustrated,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: those portions of the wire or apparatus which are highly charged will be out of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: reach, while those parts of the same which are liable to be approached, touched, or
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: handled will be at or nearly the same potential as the adjacent portions of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: ground, this insuring, both in the transmitting and receiving apparatus and regardless of the magnitude
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of the electrical pressure used, perfect personal safety, which is best evidenced by the fact
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: that although such extreme pressures of many millions of volts have been for a number
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of years continuously experimented with no injury has been sustained neither by myself or any
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of my assistants. The length of the thin-wire coil in each transformer should be approximately
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: one-quarter of the wave length of the electric disturbance in the circuit, this estimate being
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: based on the velocity of propagation of the disturbance through the coil itself and the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: circuit with which it is designed to be used. By way of illustration, if the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: rate at which the current traverses the circuit, including the coil, be one hundred and
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: eighty-five thousand miles per second, then a frequency of nine hundred and twenty-five per second
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: would maintain nine hundred and twenty-five stationary waves in a circuit one hundred and eighty-five
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: thousand miles long and each wave would be two hundred miles in length. For such
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: a low frequency, to which I shall resort only when it is indispensable to operate
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: motors of the ordinary kind under the conditions above assumed, I would use a secondary
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of fifty miles in length. By such an adjustment or proportioning of the length of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: wire in the secondary coil or coils the points of highest potential are made to
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: coincide with the elevated terminals D D', and it should be understood that whatever length
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: be given to the wires this condition should be complied with in order to attain
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the best results. As the main requirement in carrying out my invention is to produce
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: currents of an excessively-high potential, this object will be facilitated by using a primary current
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of very considerable frequency, since the electromotive force obtainable with a given length of conductor
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: is proportionate to the frequency; but the frequency of the current is in a large
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: measure arbitrary, for if the potential be sufficiently high and if the terminals of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: coils be maintained at the proper altitudes the action described will take place, and a
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: current will be transmitted through the elevated air strata, which will encounter little and possibly
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: even less resistance than if conveyed through a copper wire of a practicable size. Accordingly
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the construction of the apparatus may be in many ways greatly varied; but in order
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: to enable any person skilled in the mechanical and electrical arts to utilize to advantage
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: in the practical applications of my system the experience I have so far gained in
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the carrying out of my invention on a large scale are given. The transmitting apparatus
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: was in this case one of my electrical oscillators, which are transformers of a special
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: type, now well known and characterized by the passage of oscillatory discharges of a condenser
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: through the primary. The source G, forming one of the elements of the transmitter, was
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: a condenser of a capacity of about four one-hundredths of a microfarad and was charged
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: from a generator of alternating currents of fifty thousand volts pressure and discharged by means
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of a mechanically-operated break five thousand times per second through the primary C. The latter
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: consisted of a single turn of stout stranded cable of inappreciable resistance and of an
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: inductance of about eight thousand centimeters, the diameter of the loop being very nearly two
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: hundred and forty-four centimeters. The total inductance of the primary circuit was approximately ten thousand
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: centimeters, so that the primary circuit vibrated generally, according to adjustment, from two hundred and
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: thirty thousand to two hundred and fifty thousand times per second. The high-tension coil A
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: in the form of a flat spiral was composed of fifty turns of heavily insulated
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: cable No. 8 wound in one single layer, the turns beginning close to the primary
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: loop and ending near its center. The outer end of the secondary or high-tension coil
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: A was connected to the ground, as illustrated, while the free end was led to
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: a terminal placed in the rarefied air stratum through which the energy was to be
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: transmitted, which was contained in an insulating-tube of a length of fifty feet or more,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: within which a barometric pressure varying from about one hundred and twenty to one hundred
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and fifty millimeters was maintained by means of a mechanical suction-pump. The receiving-transformer was similarly
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: proportioned, the ratio of conversion being the reciprocal of that of the transmitter, and the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: primary high-tension coil A' was connected, as illustrated, with the end near the low-tension coil
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: C' to the ground and with the free end to a wire or plate likewise
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: placed in the rarefied air stratum and at the distance named from the transmitting-terminal. The
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: primary and secondary circuits in the transmitting apparatus being carefully synchronized, an electromotive force from
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: two to four million volts and more was obtainable at the terminals of the secondary
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: coil A, the discharge passing freely through the attenuated air stratum maintained at the above
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: barometric pressures, and it was easy under these conditions to transmit with fair economy considerable
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: amounts of energy, such as are of industrial moment, to the receiving apparatus for supplying
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: from the secondary coil C' lamps L or kindred devices. The results were particularly satisfactory
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: when the primary coil or system A', with its secondary C', was carefully adjusted, so
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: as to vibrate in synchronism with the transmitting coil or system A C. I have,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: however, found no difficulty in producing with apparatus of substantially the same design and construction
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: electromotive forces exceeding three or four times those before mentioned and have ascertained that by
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: their means current impulses can be transmitted through much-denser air strata. By the use of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: these I have also found it practicable to transmit notable amounts of energy through air
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: strata not in direct contact with the transmitting and receiving terminals, but remote from them,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the action of the impulses, in rendering conducting air of a density at which it
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: normally behaves as an insulator, extending, as before remarked, to a considerable distance. The high
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: electromotive force obtained at the terminals of coil or conductor A was, as will be
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: seen, in the preceding instance, not so much due to a large ratio of transformation
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: as to the joint effect of the capacities and inductances in the synchronized circuits, which
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: effect is enhanced by a high frequency, and it will be obviously understood that if
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the latter be reduced a greater ratio of transformation should be resorted to, especially in
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: cases in which it may be deemed of advantage to suppress as much as possible,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and particularly in the transmitting-coil A, the rise of pressure due to the above effect
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and to obtain the necessary electromotive force solely by a large transformation ratio. While electromotive
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: forces such as are produced by the apparatus just described may be sufficient for many
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: purposes to which my system will or may be applied, I wish to state that
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: I contemplate using in an industrial undertaking of this kind greatly in excess of these,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and with my present knowledge and experience in this novel field I would estimate them
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: to range from twenty to fifty million volts and possibly more. By the use of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: these much greater forces larger amounts of energy may be conveyed through the atmosphere to
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: remote places or regions, and the distance of transmission may be thus extended practically without
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: limit. As to the elevation of the terminals D D', it is obvious that it
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: will be determined by a number of things, as by the amount and quality of
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the work to be performed, by the local density and other conditions of the atmosphere,
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: by the character of the surrounding country, and such considerations as may present themselves in
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: individual instances. Thus if there be high mountains in the vicinity the terminals should be
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: at a greater height, and generally they should always be, if practicable, at altitudes much
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: greater than those of the highest objects near them in order to avoid as much
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: as possible the loss by leakage. In some cases when small amounts of energy are
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: required the high elevation of the terminals, and more particularly of the receiving-terminal D', may
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: not be necessary, since, especially when the frequency of the currents is very high, a
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: sufficient amount of energy may be collected at that terminal by electrostatic induction from the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: upper air strata, which are rendered conducting by the active terminal of the transmitter or
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: through which the currents from the same are conveyed. With reference to the facts which
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: have been pointed out above it will be seen that the altitudes required for the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: transmission of considerable amounts of electrical energy in accordance with this method are such as
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: are easily accessible and at which terminals can be safely maintained, as by the aid
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of captive balloons supplied continuously with gas from reservoirs and held in position securely by
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: steel wires or by any other means, devices, or expedients, such as may be contrived
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: and perfected by ingenious and skilled engineers. From my experiments and observations I conclude that
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: with electromotive impulses not greatly exceeding fifteen or twenty million volts the energy of many
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: thousands of horse-power may be transmitted over vast distances, measured by many hundreds and even
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: thousands of miles, with terminals not more than thirty to thirty-five thousand feet above the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: level of the sea, and even this comparatively-small elevation will be required chiefly for reasons
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: of economy, and, if desired, it may be considerably reduced, since by such means as
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: have been described practically any potential that is desired may be obtained, the currents through
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: the air strata may be rendered very small, whereby the loss in the transmission may
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: be reduced. What I now claim is— 1. The method hereinbefore described of transmitting electrical
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: energy through the natural media, which consists in producing at a generating-station a very high
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: electrical pressure, causing thereby a propagation or flow of electrical energy, by conduction, through the
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: earth and the air strata, and collecting or receiving at a distant point the electrical
attributes.document_title: Tesla System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (1897)

attributes.text: NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing at the borough of Manhattan, in

attributes.text: the city, county and State of New York, have invented certain new and useful Improvements

attributes.text: reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part of the same. This
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: application is a division of an application filed by me on September 2, 1897, Serial
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: No. 650,343, entitled "Systems of transmission of electrical energy," and is based upon new and
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: useful features and combinations of apparatus shown and described in said application for carrying out
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the method therein disclosed and claimed. The invention which forms the subject of my present
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: application comprises a transmitting coil or conductor in which electrical currents or oscillations are produced
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: and which is arranged to cause such currents or oscillations to be propagated by conduction
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: through the natural medium from one point to another remote therefrom and a receiving coil
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: or conductor adapted to be excited by the oscillations or currents propagated from the transmitter.
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: This apparatus is shown in the accompanying drawing, which is a diagrammatic illustration of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: same. A is a coil, generally of many turns and a very large diameter, wound
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: in spiral form either about a magnetic core or not, as may be desired. C
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: is a second coil formed by a conductor of much larger size and smaller length
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: wound around and in proximity to the coil A. The apparatus at one point is
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: used as a transmitter, the coil A in this case constituting a high-tension secondary, and
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the coil C the primary, of much lower tension, of a transformer. In the circuit
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: of the primary C is included a suitable source of current G. One terminal of
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the secondary A is at the center of the spiral coil, and from this terminal
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the current is led by a conductor B to a terminal D, preferably of large
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: surface, formed or maintained by such means as a balloon at an elevation suitable for
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the purposes of transmission. The other terminal of the secondary A is connected to earth
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: and, if desired, to the primary also, in order that the latter may be at
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: substantially the same potential as the adjacent portions of the secondary, thus insuring safety. At
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the receiving-station a transformer of similar construction is employed; but in this case the longer
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: coil A' constitutes the primary, and the shorter coil C' the secondary, of the transformer.
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: In the circuit of the latter are connected lamps L, motors M, or other devices
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: for utilizing the current. The elevated terminal D' connects with the center of the coil
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: A', and the other terminal of said coil is connected to earth and preferably, also,
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: to the coil C' for the reasons above stated. The length of the thin wire
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: coil in each transformer should be approximately one-quarter of the wave length of the electric
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: disturbance in the circuit, this estimate being based on the velocity of propagation of the
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: disturbance through the coil itself and the circuit with which it is designed to be
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: used. By way of illustration, if the rate at which the current traverses the circuit
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: including the coil be one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles per second then a frequency
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: of nine hundred and twenty-five per second would maintain nine hundred and twenty-five stationary waves
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: in a circuit one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles long and each wave would be
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: two hundred miles in length. For such a low frequency, which would be resorted to
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: only when it is indispensable for the operation of motors of the ordinary kind under
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the conditions above assumed, I would use a secondary of fifty miles in length. By
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: such an adjustment or proportioning of the length of wire in the secondary coil or
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: coils the points of highest potential are made to coincide with the elevated terminals D
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: D', and it should be understood that whatever length be given to the wires this
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: requirement should be complied with in order to obtain the best results. It will be
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: readily understood that when the above-prescribed relations exist the best conditions for resonance between the
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: transmitting and receiving circuits are attained, and owing to the fact that the points of
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: highest potential in the coils or conductors A A' are coincident with the elevated terminals
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the maximum flow of current will take place in the two coils, and this, further,
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: necessarily implies that the capacity and inductance in each of the circuits have such values
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: as to secure the most perfect condition of synchronism with the impressed oscillations. When the
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: source of current G is in operation and produces rapidly pulsating or oscillating currents in
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the circuit of coil C, corresponding induced currents of very much higher potential are generated

attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: the number of turns toward the center and the difference of potential between the adjacent
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: turns is comparatively small a very high potential impracticable with ordinary coils may be successively
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: current of excessively high potential, this object is facilitated by using a primary current of

attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (1900)

attributes.text: concern: Be it known that I, NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing

attributes.text: in the borough of Manhattan, in the city, county, and State of New York, have

attributes.text: following is a specification, reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part

attributes.text: of the same. In endeavoring to adapt currents or discharges of very high tension to
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: various valuable uses, as the distribution of energy through wires from central plants to distant
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: places of consumption, or the transmission of powerful disturbances to great distances, through the natural
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: or non-artificial media, I have encountered difficulties in confining considerable amounts of electricity to the
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: conductors and preventing its leakage over their supports, or its escape into the ambient air,
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: which always takes place when the electric surface density reaches a certain value. The intensity
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: of the effect of a transmitting circuit with a free or elevated terminal is proportionate
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: to the quantity of electricity displaced, which is determined by the product of the capacity
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: of the circuit, the pressure, and the frequency of the currents employed. To produce an
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: electrical movement of the required magnitude it is desirable to charge the terminal as highly
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: as possible, for while a great quantity of electricity may also be displaced by a
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: large capacity charged to low pressure, there are disadvantages met with in many cases when
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: the former is made too large. The chief of these are due to the fact
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: that an increase of the capacity entails a lowering of the frequency of the impulses
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: or discharges and a diminution of the energy of vibration. This will be understood when
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: it is borne in mind, that a circuit with a large capacity behaves as a
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: slack spring, whereas one with a small capacity acts like a stiff spring, vibrating more
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: vigorously. Therefore, in order to attain the highest possible frequency, which for certain purposes is
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: advantageous and, apart from that, to develop the greatest energy in such a transmitting circuit,
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: I employ a terminal of relatively small capacity, which I charge to as high a
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: pressure as practicable. To accomplish this result I have found it imperative to so construct
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: the elevated conductor, that its outer surface, on which the electrical charge chiefly accumulates, has
attributes.document_title: Tesla Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Wardenclyffe, 1902)

attributes.text: 20, 2018 ABSTRACT Disclosed are various embodiments for transmitting and receiving energy conveyed in the

attributes.text: form of a guided surface-waveguide mode along the surface of a lossy medium such as,
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: e.g., a terrestrial medium excited by a guided surface waveguide probe. BACKGROUND For over a
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: century, signals transmitted by radio waves involved radiation fields launched using conventional antenna structures. In
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: contrast to radio science, electrical power distribution systems in the last century involved the transmission
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: of energy guided along electrical conductors. This understanding of the distinction between radio frequency (RF)
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: and power transmission has existed since the early 1900's. KEY DISTINCTION: GUIDED vs RADIATED WAVES
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: Guided electromagnetic fields: a propagating electromagnetic wave whose energy is concentrated within or near boundaries
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: between media having different electromagnetic properties. In this sense, a guided electromagnetic field is one
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: that is bound to a waveguide and may be characterized as being conveyed by the
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: current flowing in the waveguide. If there is no load for a guided electromagnetic wave,
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: then no energy is consumed. Radiated electromagnetic fields: electromagnetic energy that is emitted from a
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: source structure in the form of waves that are not bound to a waveguide. Radiated
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: electromagnetic fields are characterized by free electromagnetic fields that emanate from the source structure and
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: spread out in space. Once radiated, these waves propagate independently of the receiver and are
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: lost regardless of whether a receiver is present. The surface wave in the Zenneck-Sommerfeld guided
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: wave sense is distinct from ground wave propagation in the Weyl-Norton-FCC sense. FREQUENCY SPECIFICATIONS Example
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: operating frequency: 1.85 MHz. At 1.85 MHz the free-space wavelength is approximately 162 meters. The
attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: guided surface wave probe is designed to match the complex Brewster angle at this frequency.

attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.document_title: Corum CPG Technologies Guided Surface Waves (2015)

attributes.text: have obtained Provisional Protection in Great Britain, by Letters Patent No. 12,039, dated June 2,
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: 1896,) of which the following is a specification. According to this invention electrical actions or
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: manifestations are transmitted through the air, earth, or water by means of electric oscillations of
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: high frequency. The apparatus employed at the transmitting-station consists of an induction-coil or equivalent means
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: for producing electric oscillations and a radiator for directing the oscillations through the air. The
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: radiator comprises a metallic surface or plate elevated above the ground and connected to one
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: terminal of the spark-gap of the induction-coil. The other terminal of the spark-gap is connected
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: to the earth. When the induction-coil is excited sparks pass across the spark-gap and electric
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: oscillations are set up in the circuit comprising the elevated plate and the earth connection.
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: These oscillations cause the emission of electromagnetic waves which are propagated outward through space. At
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the receiving-station a similar arrangement of elevated plate and earth connection is employed, connected to
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: a coherer or other detector responsive to the incoming electromagnetic waves. The electromagnetic waves striking
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the receiving plate induce oscillatory currents therein which actuate the detector. Figure 1 of the
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: accompanying drawings shows the transmitting apparatus. A is an induction-coil of any suitable type. B
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: is the spark-gap across which sparks pass when the coil is excited. One terminal of
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the spark-gap is connected to a metallic plate C elevated above the ground on a
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: pole or mast. The other terminal is connected to a metal plate D buried in
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the earth or otherwise connected to earth. Figure 2 shows the receiving apparatus. E is
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: a coherer of the Branly type comprising a glass tube containing metal filings. F is
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the receiving plate elevated on a pole. G is the earth connection. H is a
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: battery and relay for operating a signaling device J such as a Morse inker. The
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: action of the apparatus is as follows. When sparks pass in the transmitting spark-gap electromagnetic
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: waves are emitted in all directions. Those waves which strike the receiving plate induce currents
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: which cause the metal filings in the coherer to cohere and become conducting. The current
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: from the battery then flows through the coherer and the relay, and the relay operates
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: the signaling device. The range of transmission depends upon the height of the transmitting and
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: receiving plates, the power of the induction-coil, and the sensitivity of the coherer. With the
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: apparatus described signals have been transmitted over distances of several miles. For improved transmission over
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: longer distances the elevated plates may be replaced by vertical wires or antennae, and the
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: induction-coil may be replaced by a transformer of higher power. The electromagnetic waves radiated from
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: such an apparatus propagate in all directions with decreasing intensity as the distance from the
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: transmitter increases. The electromagnetic waves produced by the apparatus are of the Hertzian type, being
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: electromagnetic radiation capable of propagating through free space. The waves are detected by their effect
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: on the coherer at the receiving station, which is caused to become conducting by the
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: electromagnetic impulse of the arriving wave. I claim— 1. Improvements in transmitting electrical impulses and
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: signals through the air, earth or water by means of electric oscillations consisting of an
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: apparatus at the transmitting-station comprising an induction-coil, a spark-gap, and an elevated radiator connected to
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: one terminal of the spark-gap and an earth connection connected to the other terminal. 2.
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: Apparatus for receiving electrical signals transmitted through the air, earth or water by means of
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: electric oscillations, comprising an elevated receiving-plate, an earth connection, a coherer or equivalent detector connected
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: between the plate and the earth, and means for indicating the action of the coherer.
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: 3. The combination with a transmitting-apparatus comprising an induction-coil, a spark-gap, an elevated radiator and
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: an earth connection, of a receiving-apparatus comprising an elevated receiving-plate, an earth connection, a coherer,
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: and a signaling device operated by the coherer. 4. A method of transmitting electrical signals
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: through the air, earth or water which consists in producing electric oscillations at a transmitting-station
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: and causing said oscillations to be radiated as electromagnetic waves, and detecting said waves at
attributes.document_title: Marconi Transmitting Electrical Signals (1896, control)

attributes.text: a receiving-station by means of a coherer or similar detector. GUGLIELMO MARCONI. Witnesses: CHARLES W.
